subject: Hosted API — Intermittent request failures (BrightBridge) — customer update
messages:
From: laura.bennett@redwood.inference
To: Samir Khan <samir@brightbridge.ai>
Cc: evelyn.hart@redwood.inference, marissa.cole@redwood.inference
Date: 2027-03-04T09:42:00Z
Subject: Hosted API — Intermittent request failures (BrightBridge) — customer update

Samir,

We observed intermittent 5xx failures (primarily 502/503) affecting BrightBridge traffic to our hosted text-generation endpoints in us-west between ~08:50–09:15 PT this morning. I wanted to reach out with an immediate customer-facing summary and next steps while we continue to stabilize.

What happened (short):
- Impact: ~3–6% of BrightBridge requests returned 502/503; some streaming sessions were truncated.
- Scope: routed through us-west hostpool; other regions were largely unaffected.
- Root cause (working hypothesis): rapid control-plane route churn caused a subset of requests to be forwarded to instances still draining their KV cache, which triggered upper-layer timeouts and proxy 502s.

Mitigations we applied (in-flight):
1) Enabled short-term routing pin for BrightBridge to an isolated hostpool with warmed KV caches.
2) Triggered rolling restarts of 6 candidates showing high drain counts.
3) Increased autoscale headroom for dedicated hostpool in us-west to reduce scheduling pressure.

Customer-facing actions I propose now:
- Immediate notice to BrightBridge summarizing the above and offering a credit for hours of degraded service (TBD by finance).
- Publish a concise status page incident entry (I have a draft attached).
- Send a post-incident summary within 24 hours.

Attachments: incident-metrics-03-04.csv (sample error rates by minute), statuspage-draft.html (short summary for status.redwood).

Ask: Evelyn / Marissa — can you confirm the routing pin is holding and share a short blameless root cause once we have kernel-level logs? I can send the customer the draft status note as soon as you confirm.

Apologies for the disruption — we know BrightBridge has a tight SLA window. I will keep you posted with a consolidated timeline and artifacts.

—
Laura Bennett
Senior Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Subject: Post-incident summary: 2027-03-04 BrightBridge request failures (us-west)

Samir — following up with the post-incident summary and next steps. Thank you for your patience.

Summary (what happened):
- Between 08:50–09:15 PT on 2027-03-04, BrightBridge traffic experienced intermittent 502/503 responses affecting an estimated 3–6% of requests. The root cause was a short window of control-plane routing churn coinciding with instance drain/rehydration of KV caches.

Impact: partial request failure and some truncated streaming sessions for BrightBridge only. No data loss or credential exposure. We observed no double-billing for tokens — accounting confirmed only successful completions were billed; failed requests were not charged.

Actions taken:
- Immediate routing pin to warmed hostpool (reduced failed requests within 5 minutes).
- Rolling restarts on 6 affected instances.
- Increased autoscale buffer for us-west hostpool to prevent scheduling pressure during warmup.
- Full trace and metric export attached as postmortem-summary-03-04.pdf.

Planned preventive work:
1) Control-plane change: introduce a 15s warm-handoff where KV caches are pre-warmed before routing cutover. Target: deploy to us-west canary by 2027-03-18.
2) Observability: add a routing-change alert that correlates drain counts with 5xx spikes. Target: 2027-03-11.
3) Credits: Marissa proposed a goodwill credit equivalent to 6 hours of service at account tier II; finance will confirm and we will apply the credit within the next billing cycle.

Artifacts and links: postmortem-summary-03-04.pdf (attached), public incident page: https://status.redwood.inference/incidents/2027-03-04-brightbridge-bridge-interrupt, internal ops log: https://drive.redwood.inference/BRIGHTBRIDGE/BR-987-ops-log

If you want a short call to walk through traces, Evelyn and I are available tomorrow 10–11 PT. Otherwise we will consider this the formal post-incident summary and apply the credit once finance confirms.

Thanks again — we take this seriously and will keep working to prevent recurrence.

—
Laura Bennett
Senior Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
